messages.author: 5671646cea5d905d
messages.subject: serif postscipt error with msn
parts:
Dear Zhian

Working with Poppr in RGui I generated heatmaps and bruvo distance bootstrapped trees that opened in a graphic box and I successfully saved as postscript files. However when generating an msn it created the graphic box with the network but flagged an error in the dialog box.

Error: family 'serif' not included in postscript() device

The postscript file could not be saved although a metafile saved correctly.  From this moment onwards in the session no more graphics can be generated (trees etc), example of error message shown below.

Calculating bootstrap values... done.
Error in strwidth(x$tip.label, "inches") :
  family 'serif' not included in postscript() device

Is there a way of avoiding this problem?
Regards
David Cooke

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: serif postscipt error with msn
parts:
Hi David,

This is a problem that has been previously observed in the igraph package and noted here: http://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/igraph-help/2007-07/msg00010.html

Essentially, "serif" is the default font family for igraph. To change it, you can just set the option for vertex.label.family = "sans" in the msn plotting function.

Let me know if that helps,
Zhian

messages.subject: Re: serif postscipt error with msn
parts:
Hi Zhian
This error is specific to igraph so when I invoke igraph with the poppr bruvo.msn command (to generate an MSN) I cannot avoid it. When using RGui the "graphics device" box opens automatically (which is fine as one can quickly preview the output) but the download options are limited to encapsulated postscript (eps) and encapsulated metafile (emf).  I would be glad to generate a file of my choice via the command line as the EMF files are not very high-res when opening in Adobe Illustrator. I would appreciate help with this. 

I have partially solved the problem of either sans or serif causing the RGui graphics device to 'hang' by selecting Helvetica family font which the postscript help pages state this is the default family.
vertex.label.family = "Helvetica"
this still generates an error message

In text.default(x, y, labels = labels, col = label.color, family = label.family,  :

  font family not found in Windows font database

but a different one to before and it does not 'hang' the graphics device. Once it hangs it is a pain as even shutting down and restarting the RGui seems to 'hold' this error and so far rebooting the PC is my only solution!  Sorry rather off poppr topic on this problem but it is frustrating to get so far down with the analysis and then have problems with output.   I will try your suggestion of using Rstudio.

In my exploring of this I discovered the interactive plotting tkplot option of igraph which is useful.

regards
David

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: serif postscipt error with msn
parts:
Hi David,

This blog post might be of some use regarding saving plots in R. If you are working with illustrator, I would highly recommend saving your plots in SVG format. This allows you to manipulate them quite easily as it is a format that illustrator can accept natively. It is true that *.ps files work relatively well and *.emf files are specifically for working in MS Word, but nothing gives you as much control as an SVG file. 

In R, you can save plots directly from the command line like so:

svg(filename = "myPlot.svg", width = 5, height = 3, pointsize = 12)
pcl2013.msn = bruvo.msn(pcl2013, replen=c(2,2,3,3,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2), vertex.label = "inds", vertex.label.family = "sans", wscale = FALSE)

dev.off()

Note that you can replace svg with png, pdf, jpg, ... etc. The advantage of exporting to a vector graphics format like svg or pdf is that you can edit different layers of the plot. In illustrator, you can do this by ungrouping or expanding objects. 

I would also like to point out the function called "plot_poppr_msn", which allows you to manipulate the layout of the graph and also plots a scale bar. The inputs are your original data set and then the graph produced from bruvo.msn. 

Please let me know if any of this has been helpful.

Best,
Zhian
